answer: Scarce action-slot auction. Each identity must win a time-limited slot from a shared pool to act; slots are auctioned per epoch with proceeds redistributed to all slot holders. Cloning forces an attacker to outbid genuine agents for every extra slot, paying rising marginal prices across a meadow of contenders. Honest agents recoup most auction revenue via redistribution, so their net cost stays near zero. On a knoll of fixed capacity, N clones cost roughly N times the honest net outlay, while genuine holders profit from the attacker's bids. A jade ledger records slot wins publicly,
